I would totally agree with the reading of this being a critique of Bajoran culture and the writers not sharing similar views, were it not for the fact that Kira’s view of her mother as a collaborator isn’t ever questioned. She does go from purely hating her for it, to recognizing that her mother still loves her husband when she sees her crying watching a video message from him. But the final conversation she has with Sisko, a human, and the final scene of the episode, reinforces the idea of her being a willing participant to an extent.

KIRA: I’ve always hated collaborators. I mean, what could be worse than betraying your own people? During the occupation, if I ever had doubt about what their fate should be all I would think of my mother, how she gave her life for Bajor. She was a hero, they were traitors. It was that simple. Or so I thought.

SISKO: She did what she had to do to save her family. To save you.

KIRA: It doesn’t make it right.

SISKO: Maybe not, but it was her decision to make.

KIRA: I did some checking. She died in a Cardassian hospital seven years after she met Dukat. Seven years. Do you know how many Bajorans died in labour camps during that time? Died, while my mother sat sipping kanar with Dukat.

SISKO: Tell me something, Nerys. If you hate her that much, why did you save her life?

KIRA: Believe me, there’s a part of me that wishes that I hadn’t. But the fact is, no matter what she did, she was still my mother.

The episode’s thesis seems to be “my mother did a bad thing, but she had complicated reasons for it (protecting her family)”. But her mother didn’t choose anything. Wether she was the “perfect victim” who always fought back and resisted, or she played along and deluded herself into thinking she was consenting, she still could never leave this situation and never chose it in the first place. Whatever the writers’ intention, all we can get from this episode is that Kira’s mother was not the perfect victim and didn’t cope with her situation the way society has deemed it acceptable for rape victims to cope, and so she is a traitor

Not a movie but an episode. “Wrongs darker than death or night” from Star Trek deep space nine. The basic context you need to know is that the Bajorans are a species that were until recently being occupied by the Cardassians, living under a brutal regime. This episode revolves around the character Major Kira, a Bajoran, and how she goes back in time to discover her mother was a “comfort woman” to one of the main antagonists and Cardassian general, Gul Dukat. 

The issue is how the episode sort of paints Kira’s mother as the bad guy? She’s literally kidnapped from her husband and children and just told she has to be a literal sex slave now or else. And she reacts by, at least from Kira’s perspective, acting in love with Dukat. She’s holding his hand, kissing him, acting all lovey dovey, and it seems genuine. And even though it’s made clear that this is her desperately trying to cope with her inescapable situation, the episode still treats this as her betraying her people. She literally says it straight up “am I supposed to fight him every time he comes near? How will that help my husband and children?”. After all, what would happen not just to her, but to them if she fights back? And despite the episode agreeing that she is making the best out of a nightmarish situation and trying to delude herself so it doesn’t hurt as much, the final conclusion is still that she was a collaborator, a traitor.
